methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a clearly defined multiphase design: a large retrospective multicenter evaluation (115,973 mammograms from five services with 39-month follow-up) plus a prospective noninterventional feasibility deployment (9,266 cases across 12 sites). The primary endpoint is prespecified as noninferiority of AI versus first reader for sensitivity and specificity with a 5% margin, and the analysis uses paired/cluster-aware methods (Wald intervals/tests with Obuchowski variance; Holm-Bonferroni correction; clustered McNemar extension for superiority) appropriate to screening reads. A key implementation limitation is that data collection/analysis were not blinded and the prospective phase required threshold recalibration after a distribution shift, but both are explicitly reported and operationalized.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an observational diagnostic/workflow performance study with prospective technical feasibility rather than a randomized trial, fitting Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is very high because it quantifies changes in cancer detection and workload at population screening scale (for example, higher cancer detection rate and interval/next-round cancer identification) and directly addresses equity/fairness and real deployment issues such as drift and recalibration.

reporting_quality.justification: STARD is the closest reporting standard given the diagnostic accuracy framing, and the manuscript reports cohort inclusion/exclusion, follow-up ground truth, prespecified endpoints and margins, and detailed statistical testing including multiplicity correction. The prospective feasibility phase is described with explicit monitoring and adaptive operating-point recalibration after observed recall-rate shifts. Data sharing appears limited to statistical "Source Data" for figures/tables in the normalized text, with no clear open repository for underlying screening data or analysis code.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty lies in combining a large multicenter retrospective evaluation with a real prospective (noninterventional) feasibility deployment, explicitly confronting distribution shift and ongoing calibration/monitoring requirements. The work goes beyond standalone AI ROC claims by quantifying screening outcomes such as cancer detection rate, interval/next-round cancer identification, reader-time savings, and exploratory fairness analyses. It is still an extension of an existing AI system rather than a new algorithmic class, keeping it below a field-defining score.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured by phase, with explicit primary/secondary endpoints and quantitative abstract reporting (sensitivities/specificities, detection rates, and follow-up windows). Methods and results use consistent terminology (operating point selection, noninferiority/superiority testing, subgroup analyses) and the figure captions are numerically specific. Some methodological density is unavoidable, but overall presentation supports auditability.

key_strengths: Large multicenter retrospective evaluation with long follow-up ground truth (115,973 mammograms; 39 months) paired with prospective feasibility deployment (9,266 cases; 12 sites)
Prespecified noninferiority design with multiplicity control and cluster-aware paired testing aligned to screening-read structure
Clinically meaningful endpoints beyond accuracy (cancer detection rate changes, interval/next-round cancer identification, simulated reading-time reduction)
Explicit handling of real-world deployment risk: observed distribution shift and operating-point recalibration with continuous monitoring
key_concerns: Prospective phase demonstrates drift/distribution shift requiring recalibration, underscoring the need for strong governance/monitoring in any real deployment
Some subgroup results are underpowered and borderline/noninferior in small groups, limiting strength of equity conclusions despite the overall size
Reproducibility posture is only partially visible in the blinded text (statistical source data noted, but no explicit open data/code)
chief_reviewer.rationale: The combination of scale, prespecified paired noninferiority statistics, and a prospective feasibility phase that surfaces calibration challenges makes this a top-tier, implementation-relevant screening AI paper. Minor revisions would mainly target clearer reproducibility commitments and tighter framing of subgroup/fairness conclusions given small-n uncertainty in some strata.
